title: How people opt in to texts from Yuppers.app
description: Each step a person takes to receive text messages from Yuppers.app, with the exact wording of every screen and message.
intro: Yuppers.app (https://yuppers.app) has one text-message program, Yuppers.app agreement updates, and sends no marketing. This page shows each step a person takes to receive those updates, with a picture of each screen and the exact wording it shows. One-time codes sent by text, to sign in, to confirm a phone number or to confirm deleting an account, are sent and checked by our provider Twilio’s verification service, Twilio Verify; they are not part of the agreement-updates program, and their forms are shown in a section of their own after it.
note: On yuppers.app and in the Yuppers mobile app, the “Text updates” control on an agreement, signing in with a phone number and a code by text to delete an account appear only while texting is turned on for the service. The screens below show them as they appear when texting is enabled.
websiteIntro: These screens were captured from the Yuppers website, https://yuppers.app, on a phone-sized screen.
mobileIntro: The Yuppers app for iPhone and Android has the same “Text updates” control on an agreement, with the same box and the same wording. Each picture is the whole screen, under the app’s own navigation bar.
mobileRelease: The Yuppers app is not yet published in the App Store or Google Play, so these pictures were taken from the app’s own screens, built from its code and shown at the size of an iPhone screen, rather than from a store download.
mobileSame: The consent wording, the opt-in confirmation text and the HELP and STOP replies are the same on the website and in the app.
programs: Yuppers.app agreement updates: one text per status change of an agreement the person turned updates on for, and one text confirming that they turned them on. Message frequency varies; there is no fixed maximum.
codesNote: One-time codes by text are not part of this program. They are sent and checked by Twilio Verify, from Twilio’s own senders, and are shown below under “One-time codes”.
codesHeading: One-time codes (sent by Twilio Verify, not part of the agreement-updates program)
codesIntro: Three forms text a one-time code: signing in with a phone number, confirming a phone number added to an account, and confirming that an account is to be deleted. Each code is sent and checked by our provider Twilio’s verification service, Twilio Verify, one message per request, and only once the person ticks the box beside the number. These texts are not part of the Yuppers.app agreement updates program.

agreementUpdates.heading: Agreement updates
agreementUpdates.intro: Text updates are turned on one agreement at a time, with a box on that agreement, and a text confirms it. The account needs a phone number first; adding one is shown under “Confirming a phone number” in the one-time codes’ section.

replies.heading: HELP and STOP
replies.intro: Replying HELP or STOP to any text from the agreement-updates number is answered at once with these texts. STOP ends every text from Yuppers.app to that number, agreement updates and one-time codes alike, until it replies START; the person can still sign in with an email address. Each agreement update looks like the last text below.

signIn.heading: Signing in by text
signIn.intro: The sign-in form, the first screen for anyone not signed in. A code is texted only to a number the person types there, and only once they tick the box beside it.

confirmNumber.heading: Confirming a phone number
confirmNumber.intro: Text updates need a US mobile number on the account. If it has none, “Text updates” on an agreement first asks for one and checks that it is the person’s with a one-time code, sent by Twilio Verify only once they tick the box beside the number.

deleteAccount.heading: Deleting an account by text
deleteAccount.intro: Deleting an account is confirmed with a one-time code sent to the account’s email address or phone number. When it is to go to the phone number, it is texted only once the person ticks the box beside it. The pictures show an account whose only way in is its phone number.

signIn.title: Step 1. Entering a phone number to sign in
signIn.caption: The sign-in form takes an email address or a phone number. As soon as what is typed reads as a phone number, an unticked box appears beside the consent text below, whose two addresses are links to the terms and the privacy policy. “Send code” stays disabled until the box is ticked, and the form says why. Under the button are links to the section on text messages in the privacy policy, to the privacy policy and to the terms.
signIn.alt: The Yuppers sign-in form on a phone, with a phone number entered, an unticked box beside the consent text with links to the terms and the privacy policy, the Send code button disabled, and the line saying to tick the box first.

boxTicked.title: Step 2. Ticking the box
boxTicked.caption: Once the person ticks the box, “Send code” is enabled. Pressing it asks for one text with a sign-in code; nothing is sent before.
boxTicked.alt: The same sign-in form with the box beside the consent text ticked and the Send code button enabled.

codeSent.title: Step 3. After asking for a code
codeSent.caption: The screen says where the code went and asks for it. The text that carries the code is shown below the picture.
codeSent.alt: The Yuppers sign-in form after a code was sent: the number it went to, and a field for the six-digit code.

confirmNumber.title: Step 1. Entering the number to add
confirmNumber.caption: On an agreement the person is a party to, when their account has no phone number, “Text updates” asks for a US mobile number, with an unticked box beside the consent text below, whose two addresses are links to the terms and the privacy policy. “Text me a code” stays disabled until the box is ticked, and the form says why.
confirmNumber.alt: The Text updates section of an agreement on a phone, asking for a mobile number, with a number entered, an unticked box beside the consent text with links to the terms and the privacy policy, the Text me a code button disabled, and the line saying to tick the box first.

confirmNumberTicked.title: Step 2. Ticking the box
confirmNumberTicked.caption: Once the person ticks the box, “Text me a code” is enabled. Pressing it asks for one text with a code that confirms the number; nothing is sent before. Changing the number unticks the box.
confirmNumberTicked.alt: The same Text updates section with the box beside the consent text ticked and the Text me a code button enabled.

confirmNumberCodeSent.title: Step 3. After asking for a code
confirmNumberCodeSent.caption: The form says which number the code went to, partly hidden, and asks for it. Entering it adds the number to the account, and the agreement’s own box follows (“Agreement updates” below). The text that carries the code is shown below the picture.
confirmNumberCodeSent.alt: The Text updates section after a code was sent: the number it went to, partly hidden, and a field for the code from the text.

deleteAccount.title: Step 1. Asking to delete the account
deleteAccount.caption: On the account page, “Delete my account” first says what deleting does, then that a one-time code will be sent to the account’s phone number, with an unticked box beside the consent text below, whose two addresses are links to the terms and the privacy policy. “Send code and continue” stays disabled until the box is ticked, and the form says why. A code sent to an email address needs no box.
deleteAccount.alt: The end of the account deletion form on a phone: the number the code will go to, an unticked box beside the consent text with links to the terms and the privacy policy, the Send code and continue button disabled, and the line saying to tick the box first.

deleteAccountTicked.title: Step 2. Ticking the box
deleteAccountTicked.caption: Once the person ticks the box, “Send code and continue” is enabled. Pressing it asks for one text with a code that works only for deleting the account; nothing is sent before.
deleteAccountTicked.alt: The same deletion form with the box beside the consent text ticked and the Send code and continue button enabled.

deleteAccountCodeSent.title: Step 3. After asking for a code
deleteAccountCodeSent.caption: The form says where the code went and asks for it. Nothing is deleted until the person enters the code and confirms once more. The text that carries the code is shown below the picture.
deleteAccountCodeSent.alt: The deletion form after a code was sent: the number it went to, and a field for the six-digit code.

textUpdates.title: Step 1. Turning on text updates for an agreement
textUpdates.caption: On an agreement the person is a party to, once their account has a phone number, “Text updates” shows an unticked box beside the consent wording below, whose two addresses are links to the terms and the privacy policy. Nothing is sent unless the person ticks the box and presses Save.
textUpdates.alt: The Text updates section of an agreement on a phone: an unticked box beside the consent wording, with links to the terms and the privacy policy, and a Save button.

confirmation.title: Step 2. After ticking the box and saving
confirmation.caption: The screen confirms that text updates are on for this agreement, says how often and to which number they go, and how to stop them.
confirmation.alt: The Text updates section after saving: the box ticked, and the confirmation that text updates are on, with the number partly hidden.

replies.help: Yuppers.app: Text updates about agreements you turned updates on for. Help: support@yuppers.app or https://yuppers.app/help. Msg & data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out.
replies.stop: Yuppers.app: You're unsubscribed and will get no more texts from us. You can still sign in with your email address. Reply START to resubscribe.
